ts_jobs.verdict: FAIL on its own terms, correctly
ts_jobs.note: The probe reported rc=0, cuda_malloc=ok, launch=ok, device=NVIDIA GeForce RTX 5090 -- and result_correct=FALSE. That was MY bug: the kernel doubled uninitialised device memory because the host buffer was never copied in. The probe asserted its read-back rather than trusting rc, so an unfalsifiable probe failed loudly instead of passing green. uid_tasks on this run: 1979.
Authoritative. cuda_malloc ok, launch ok, read-back correct, 0.70s wall (design budget <10s). uid_tasks on this run: 2006.

failed_job_note: The first probe job is kept rather than deleted, because it is the evidence that the fail-closed read-back assertion works. A probe that had trusted rc==0 would have gone green on a kernel reading garbage.

rejected_submission.cause: malformed submission: I wrote 'ts submit ... -- cmd', and this front end consumed the word 'submit' as the COMMAND, so the daemon tried to exec an executable named 'submit'
rejected_submission.note: Cost no GPU time, but it queued for ~40 minutes behind other tenants before failing, which is why it is recorded rather than quietly dropped.

queue_hygiene_incident.what: I ran 'ts queue', 'ts status', 'ts logs ID' and 'ts cancel ID' believing they were queries/commands. This front end accepts only ts (bare) for status, ts -c for logs, ts -k for cancel; every other leading word is taken as the COMMAND to run.
queue_hygiene_incident.consequence: six junk jobs (named 'queue', 'status', 'logs ...', 'cancel ...') were submitted into a queue shared with cclm, opguard and chessvar, three of them AHEAD of my real probe.
queue_hygiene_incident.remedy: all six cancelled with ts -k; queue verified clean afterwards
queue_hygiene_incident.recorded_because: it wasted other people's queue and the right response is to write it down, not to quietly clean up and move on

uid_task_drift_observed.why_it_matters: gpu-sim-u2o.6.1.1 bracketed this uid's live task total between 2048 (aborts the process at its first thread creation) and 3072 (works). The live count is now 2006, i.e. 42 tasks below the abort threshold, and it moved 27 tasks in two minutes. This is direct evidence for the gate's central claim that EVERY fixed RLIMIT_NPROC value is a race on this shared host -- and that 2048, which reads as a generous limit, is currently within a rounding error of killing CUDA.

note: Both jobs were submitted through ts and waited behind other tenants (cclm, conway-gode) without jumping. No nvidia-smi was used for GPU work; the probe reports the device from cudaGetDeviceProperties.
